key_insight: Oxygen changes the surface tension of AlTi alloy melts in a composition-dependent way by enriching the interface and suppressing aluminum surface segregation.
engineering_relevance: These results help predict and control melt surface behavior in oxide-exposed alloy processing, relevant to casting, additive manufacturing, and containerless experiments.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of AlTi metallic alloy melts.
Machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) for bulk and surface properties.
Element-resolved density profile analysis with oxygen present/absent.
evidence_signal: The simulation results were compared against experimental surface-tension values from levitation measurements in microgravity.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on the transferability of the MLIP to oxygen-containing interfacial conditions, so surface predictions should be validated carefully against experiment.
paper_title: The effect of oxygen on the surface tension of AlTi metallic alloys
